description: Taylor has race condition in /get-patch that allows purchase token replay
how_introduced: This AI-authored commit first introduced token_used_at, the "Purchase token has already been used." check, and the separate UPDATE purchases SET token_used_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ? after the earlier SELECT. Pickaxe search shows the token_used_at strings and the update statement originate here. That is exactly the non-atomic check-then-act pattern the fix replaced with a single conditional UPDATE, so this commit introduced the race.

bug_commits.author: google-labs-jules[bot]
bug_commits.message: Update PayPal SDK in Backend-in-a-Box and attempt dependency audit

agent_verdicts.reasoning: This commit only refactored PayPal SDK usage and order creation code. Its diff does not touch the /get-patch token-consumption logic, and blame on the vulnerable pre-fix lines attributes that hunk to earlier commits (mostly 5e5a80b5, plus older ancestry), not to 45b69f6. It was blamed because it touched the file, not because it introduced the race.

This AI-authored commit first introduced token_used_at, the "Purchase token has already been used." check, and the separate UPDATE purchases SET token_used_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ? after the earlier SELECT. Pickaxe search shows the token_used_at strings and the update statement originate here. That is exactly the non-atomic check-then-act pattern the fix replaced with a single conditional UPDATE, so this commit introduced the race.

This initial commit created /get-patch, but its implementation only did SELECT * FROM purchases ... and then returned the decrypted patch; it had no token_used_at column, no already-used check, and no UPDATE to consume the token. That means the screening hypothesis is incorrect: c139 did not introduce the non-atomic check-then-act flow fixed in fdf67a6. It introduced a more permissive reusable-token design, but not the specific race condition this CVE fix addresses.
